terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, transitive; often with alicunde, from somewhere
evidence: Ter. Ad. 2.2.34: alicunde corrādere, to scrape together from some source (Lewis & Short s.v. alicunde)
Traupman 107: I’ll try to scrape together the money, cōnābor argentum conrādere
terms.comment: Literally “to rake together”; Lewis & Short calls it rare and mostly ante- and post-classical, used chiefly of money.

phrases.english: I’ll try to scrape the money together.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 107, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
